title: Make SSDP datagram parsing total so a malformed LOCATION cannot raise
description:
## What to fix

`lib/upnp/ssdp/parser.ex:94` calls `URI.new/1` on the `LOCATION` header without any guard.

`URI.new/1` **raises** `FunctionClauseError`, originating in `:uri_string.parse_userinfo/2`, when the
host, path or userinfo contains invalid UTF-8. `URI.parse/1` does not raise on the same input. This is
the **only unguarded `URI.new` call site in the library**: `lib/upnp/xml.ex:187-196` and
`lib/upnp/xml.ex:200-212` already wrap `URI.new` in `try` and `rescue`, so the correct defensive
pattern already exists in the tree and simply was not applied to the SSDP path.

The raise propagates out of `UPnP.SSDP.parse/1` into `UPnP.SSDP.Interface`, the GenServer that owns
the UDP socket, in its `handle_info({:udp, ...})` clause. Since the interface is supervised by the
`ssdp_interfaces` DynamicSupervisor with default restart intensity, a short burst of malformed
datagrams exhausts intensity and destroys the whole control point through the `:one_for_all` runtime.

Parsing a datagram must be **total**. A datagram must never be able to raise.

## Steps to Reproduce

Reproduced against running code during the audit.

Minimal, no processes involved:

1. Build a NOTIFY datagram whose `LOCATION` header contains invalid UTF-8, for example the byte
   sequence `0xFF 0xFE` inside the host.
2. Call `UPnP.SSDP.parse/1` on it.
3. Observe `FunctionClauseError` raised from `:uri_string.parse_userinfo/2`.

Full impact, through the transport seam:

1. Start a control point with a fake `UPnP.SSDP.Transport`.
2. Deliver 4 or 5 such malformed datagrams to the interface.
3. Observe `UPnP.SSDP.Interface` crash repeatedly, the `ssdp_interfaces` DynamicSupervisor exhaust
   its intensity, and the `:one_for_all` runtime take the coordinator down with reason `:shutdown`,
   after which the control point is gone for good.

Invalid UTF-8 was independently confirmed to raise from `URI.new/1` in the host, the path and the
userinfo positions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `parse_location/1` cannot raise for any binary input, including invalid UTF-8 in host, path and
      userinfo.
- [ ] The guard follows the pattern already used in `lib/upnp/xml.ex`, using `String.valid?/1` and/or
      `try` with `rescue`, rather than introducing a third style.
- [ ] An unparsable `LOCATION` leaves the field unset instead of failing the whole datagram, matching
      the project rule that parsers only fail when a document identifies nothing.
- [ ] A property-based or table-driven test asserts that `UPnP.SSDP.parse/1` never raises across a
      corpus of malformed datagrams, covering invalid UTF-8, embedded null bytes, and truncated
      headers.
- [ ] A regression test feeds a malformed `LOCATION` datagram through the `UPnP.SSDP.Transport` test
      seam and asserts the interface process survives. It must fail before the fix.
- [ ] Audit the tree for any other unguarded `URI.new` call sites introduced since this audit.

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately

title: Bound the presence roster and its per-entry expiry timers
description:
## What to fix

`update_roster/2` in `lib/upnp/control_point.ex:560-592` keys roster entries by `Device.identity/1`,
which is a downcased UUID taken directly from the attacker-supplied `USN` header. Every unique `USN`
creates a roster entry **and** a live BEAM timer, and nothing bounds either.

`lib/upnp/options.ex` has no `max_roster_entries` option, so there is no way for an operator to cap
this. `prune_document_caches/2` at `lib/upnp/control_point.ex:863-879` runs only on boot and on config
change, never on `byebye` or on expiry, so the description and SCPD caches grow alongside the roster.

The `UPnP.ControlPoint` moduledoc currently claims a "bounded presence roster". That claim is false
and must be corrected or made true.

## Steps to Reproduce

Measured during the audit against running code.

1. Start a control point with a fake `UPnP.SSDP.Transport`.
2. Record the coordinator's heap size with `Process.info/2`.
3. Inject 50 000 alive envelopes, each with a distinct random `USN` UUID, via
   `UPnP.ControlPoint.inject/2`.
4. Record the heap size again and count outstanding timers.

Observed: the injection took **0.33 seconds** and the coordinator heap grew from **5 976 bytes to
41 051 200 bytes**, a **6 869 times** increase, with 50 000 live BEAM timers outstanding and no
eviction at any point.

The blast radius is the whole BEAM node, not just the control point, because a single process heap of
this size and a timer wheel of this depth degrade the scheduler and can exhaust node memory.

## Design notes

Eviction policy is a real decision, not an implementation detail. Consider:

- A configurable `max_roster_entries` with a documented default and a documented eviction policy.
- Per-source admission control, since the source address of the datagram is already recorded as
  `remote_endpoint` in `to_device/1` at `lib/upnp/control_point.ex:656-668`.
- Emitting telemetry or a log warning when eviction occurs, so operators can see the pressure.

Note that a related High finding, not filed as a separate issue, is that `remote_endpoint` is never
compared against `location.host`, so USNs and locations can be freely spoofed. Any admission control
added here should keep that correlation in mind.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `lib/upnp/options.ex` gains a validated `max_roster_entries` option with a documented default.
- [ ] The roster never exceeds the configured cap, and the eviction policy is documented in the
      moduledoc.
- [ ] Evicting an entry also cancels its expiry timer, so timers cannot outlive their entries.
- [ ] Document caches are pruned on `byebye` and on expiry, not only on boot and config change.
- [ ] The `UPnP.ControlPoint` moduledoc no longer claims a bounded roster unless the bound is real.
- [ ] A regression test injects more than the cap in unique USNs and asserts both the roster size and
      the live timer count stay bounded. It must fail before the fix.
- [ ] A test asserts that memory does not grow without bound under sustained unique-USN injection.

## Blocked by

bd-2cp, because roster expiry timers must already be sane before an eviction policy that interacts
with those timers is layered on top.

title: Run eventing transport operations as supervised tasks
description:
## Parent

bd-3lm

## What to build

Standardize subscribe, renew, and unsubscribe execution in `UPnP.Eventing.Subscription` on supervised task semantics. The current worker uses raw `spawn_link`, `trap_exit`, custom operation references, and manual kill handling while control-point and lease operations use `Task.Supervisor.async_nolink`.

Use the task supervisor owned by the control-point runtime from bd-2vi. Preserve manual-clock deadlines, cancellation, result normalization, and graceful versus abrupt shutdown. Do not let transport exceptions crash the subscription state machine or leave replies in its mailbox after cancellation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every outbound GENA operation runs under the owning runtime task supervisor.
- [ ] `UPnP.Eventing.Subscription` no longer requires raw `spawn_link` solely for transport work.
- [ ] Completion, task crash, timeout, cancellation, worker shutdown, and late-result races each have behavioral tests.
- [ ] Manual-clock timeout tests prove the in-flight task terminates and the expected lifecycle event is emitted.
- [ ] Graceful close attempts one bounded `UNSUBSCRIBE`; abrupt owner/runtime loss sends none.
- [ ] No task or timer remains after the subscription worker exits.

## Blocked by

- bd-2vi
close_reason: Resolved in 8e8c10c. Subscribe, renew, and unsubscribe now run under the owning control-point runtime task supervisor with bounded cancellation and late-result cleanup. Regression: test/upnp/eventing/runtime_test.exs and test/eventing_integration_test.exs.

title: Replace control-point cache white-box tests with Interface assertions
description:
## Parent

bd-3lm

## What to build

Rewrite the cache and single-flight tests in `test/description_control_test.exs` so they verify behavior through `UPnP.ControlPoint` and the fake HTTP Adapter. Remove direct GenServer wire messages and assertions against internal pending, description-cache, or SCPD-cache state.

Use concurrent public calls and observable request counts to prove coalescing, cache hits, failure eviction, and boot/config generation invalidation. Follow the deterministic synchronization conventions established by bd-l0f.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Two concurrent `ControlPoint.describe/2` calls produce exactly one HTTP request and receive the same result.
- [ ] Description and SCPD cache hits are proven by absence of additional Adapter requests.
- [ ] Timeout and parse failures are proven not to enter either cache by a successful subsequent fetch.
- [ ] A boot/config generation change is proven to force refetching through the public Interface.
- [ ] No test sends raw GenServer protocol tuples or inspects control-point state with `:sys.get_state/1`.
- [ ] Tests remain deterministic under concurrent ExUnit execution.

## Blocked by

- bd-l0f
close_reason: Resolved in cb376bb. Cache and single-flight behavior is now verified through ControlPoint and the fake HTTP Adapter without internal protocol or state access. Regression: test/description_control_interface_test.exs and test/description_control_test.exs.

title: Clamp untrusted SSDP max-age before scheduling roster expiry timers
description:
## What to fix

`lib/upnp/ssdp/parser.ex:113-126` parses `CACHE-CONTROL: max-age` with the regex fragment `(\d+)` and
applies no upper bound, so `CACHE-CONTROL: max-age=99999999999` parses successfully. The value then
flows into `lib/upnp/control_point.ex:563-566`, where `update_roster/2` computes `max_age * 1_000` and
passes it directly to `Clock.send_after`, which is `Process.send_after/3`.

The BEAM timer ceiling was measured by binary search at **9 223 372 034 557 ms**, so the smallest
crashing `max-age` is **9 223 372 035** seconds. Any larger value makes `Process.send_after/3` raise
`ArgumentError`, killing the coordinator.

Because `UPnP.ControlPoint.Runtime` is `:one_for_all` with unconfigured restart intensity (3 in 5 s)
and the coordinator is `:transient`, repeated crashes exhaust intensity, the runtime exits
`:shutdown`, and `:transient` treats `:shutdown` as a normal exit, so the control point is **never
restarted**.

Treat every duration derived from the wire as untrusted input.

## Steps to Reproduce

Reproduced twice during the audit, both against running code.

Fast path, through the test seam:

1. Start a control point with a fake `UPnP.SSDP.Transport`.
2. Monitor the coordinator returned by `UPnP.ControlPoint.whereis/1`.
3. Inject one envelope with `max_age: 9_223_372_036` via `UPnP.ControlPoint.inject/2`.
4. Observe the coordinator die with `{:badarg, [{:erlang, :send_after, ...}]}`.

Wire path, showing the full impact:

1. Start a control point and subscribe to the roster.
2. Deliver about 4 NOTIFY datagrams carrying `CACHE-CONTROL: max-age=99999999999` over about 5
   seconds.
3. Observe that the runtime is no longer alive, that the registered name resolves to `nil`, and that
   the roster subscriber's mailbox length is **0**, meaning zero notifications were delivered.

The wire parser was separately confirmed to return `max_age: 99999999999` from
`CACHE-CONTROL: max-age=99999999999`, so the bad value really does survive parsing.

## Why the test suite missed it

`mix.exs` excludes `UPnP.Clock.System` from coverage. The real clock, the module that actually
raises, is never exercised. Any fix should close that gap rather than rely on the fake clock.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `parse_max_age/1` clamps to a documented ceiling. UPnP practice is at most 86 400 seconds.
- [ ] A second defensive clamp exists immediately before the timer is scheduled in `update_roster/2`,
      so no future caller can reintroduce the crash.
- [ ] A value above the BEAM timer ceiling never reaches `Process.send_after/3`.
- [ ] The clamp is applied without raising, consistent with the project rule that parsing is total and
      lenient.
- [ ] A regression test injects an envelope with `max_age: 9_223_372_036` and asserts the coordinator
      stays alive and the roster entry is scheduled at the clamped ceiling. It must fail before the
      fix.
- [ ] A parser unit test asserts the clamped value for an absurd `CACHE-CONTROL` header, including the
      exact boundary 9 223 372 035.
- [ ] A test exercises the real `UPnP.Clock.System` on this path, or the coverage exclusion is
      narrowed so this class of defect cannot hide again.

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately
close_reason: Resolved in 78dc088. SSDP max-age is capped at 86,400 seconds during parsing and immediately before roster timer scheduling. Regression: hostile max-age parser boundaries and real UPnP.Clock.System coordinator survival.

comments.author: Christian Geuer-Pollmann
comments.text: Human decision recorded 2026-07-27: treat the single missed 100 ms delivery in unrelated test/ssdp_interface_test.exs:87 as a transient test flake after both the exact selector and the full suite passed with the same seed; finish bd-2cp after one fresh complete Definition of Done run.

title: Enforce the documented telemetry measurement contract
description:
## Parent

bd-3lm

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Attach a telemetry handler for `[:upnp, :ssdp, :datagram_dropped]`.
2. Deliver an SSDP datagram larger than the configured maximum to an interface worker through its transport seam.
3. Observe `%{bytes: size}` without the `count: 1` measurement promised by `UPnP.Telemetry` documentation.

## What to build

Make emitted telemetry match `UPnP.Telemetry` documentation. Add contract-level tests that attach a telemetry handler and assert stable measurements plus sanitized metadata for representative success and failure paths.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `[:upnp, :ssdp, :datagram_dropped]` includes both `count: 1` and the dropped byte count.
- [ ] Every event returned by `UPnP.Telemetry.events/0` is emitted with the documented required measurements.
- [ ] Tests assert that response bodies, exception payloads, and other unbounded sensitive values do not appear in metadata.
- [ ] Measurement and metadata keys are documented per event in ExDoc.
- [ ] Existing telemetry event names remain stable.

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately
close_reason: Resolved in 8b9b3e4. Telemetry emissions now enforce documented measurements and metadata while sanitizing error payloads. Regression: test/telemetry_test.exs.

title: Separate eventing routing configuration from subscription coordination
description:
## Parent

bd-3lm

## What to build

Preserve the genuine Depth of the shared GENA subscription coordinator while moving incidental callback configuration and pure URL/host routing policy out of `UPnP.Eventing.Manager`. The manager currently spans configuration aliases, listener lifecycle, callback-token routing, local subscriber bookkeeping, pending subscribe calls, and graceful worker shutdown.

Create Locality for canonical option validation and callback-origin composition without exposing new public seams. Remove undocumented synonym keys such as callback URL/bind/host aliases; unknown options should fail explicitly. Keep concurrency, atomic snapshot installation, and worker ownership behind the existing control-point/service Interface.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `UPnP.Eventing.Manager` remains responsible for shared-subscription coordination, pending callers, consumers, tokens, and worker lifecycle.
- [ ] Canonical callback configuration is parsed and validated in one internal Module with no undocumented synonyms.
- [ ] Callback URL/origin composition is pure, directly tested, and uses the route Adapter established by bd-ahf.
- [ ] Invalid or unknown manager options return explicit startup errors.
- [ ] Public behavior for lazy listener startup, token rotation, early NOTIFY handling, replay, renewal, and graceful close remains unchanged.
- [ ] Eventing tests primarily cross the `Service.subscribe/2` or manager Interface and do not add `:sys.get_state/1` assertions.

## Blocked by

- bd-1or
- bd-ahf
close_reason: Resolved in d542ad6. Manager startup now rejects unknown and noncanonical callback options while internal configuration owns validated route-aware callback URL composition. Regression: UPnP.Eventing.RuntimeTest rejects unknown and undocumented callback aliases during startup; UPnP.Eventing.ConfigurationTest directly covers routing and composition.

title: Supervise each control point as an isolated OTP runtime
description:
## Parent

bd-3lm

## What to build

Make the OTP supervision tree reflect control-point ownership. Today SSDP interfaces, eventing managers, event subscriptions, callback listeners, and task work are placed under globally named sibling supervisors in `lib/upnp/application.ex`, even though their lifetimes and failures belong to one `UPnP.ControlPoint`.

Introduce an owned runtime subtree for each control point while retaining only genuinely shared infrastructure, such as the Finch connection pool, at application scope. Preserve both supported startup paths: direct supervision with `{UPnP.ControlPoint, options}` and `UPnP.start_control_point/1`. Remove `UPnP.Registry` unless the accepted topology gives it a concrete naming responsibility.

This slice requires human review of the proposed child topology before implementation because it changes restart and failure domains.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The proposed supervision topology and restart strategies are documented and approved before code changes.
- [ ] Each control point owns its SSDP and eventing descendants in an inspectable subtree.
- [ ] Terminating or crashing one control point leaves a second control point and its descendants unaffected.
- [ ] Descendants terminate without orphan windows when their owning control point stops.
- [ ] Directly supervised and dynamically started control points preserve graceful versus abrupt shutdown semantics.
- [ ] Failure-injection tests cover child crash, owned-supervisor crash, and normal control-point close.
- [ ] The unused Registry process is removed or receives a documented, tested responsibility.

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately
close_reason: Resolved in 6cc7738. Each control point now starts a UPnP.ControlPoint.Runtime: a transient one_for_all supervisor owning the coordinator, a per-control-point Task.Supervisor, the SSDP interface supervisor, and the eventing manager, subscription and callback-server supervisors. The coordinator is a transient significant child under auto_shutdown: :any_significant, so crashes restart the runtime coherently while graceful close stops it without restart. Application scope keeps only Finch, the registry, the runtime roots and IGD leases. UPnP.Registry now resolves {runtime id, component} to owned processes, backing ControlPoint.whereis/1 and runtime/1 so runtime handles, coordinator pids and names stay interchangeable across both startup paths. Regression: test/control_point_runtime_test.exs, twelve failure-injection and lifecycle tests including interface restart-storm isolation between two control points, which fails before the fix because the shared interface supervisor took the second control point's interface down with it.

comments.author: Christian Geuer-Pollmann
comments.text:
Human decision approved on 2026-07-26:

Adopt one isolated `UPnP.ControlPoint.Runtime` supervisor per control point. The runtime root is transient and uses `:one_for_all`. It owns the control-point coordinator, a per-control-point `Task.Supervisor`, the SSDP interface `DynamicSupervisor`, and the eventing manager, subscription, and callback-server supervisors. A crash of the coordinator or an owned supervisor restarts that runtime coherently without affecting another control point; leaf workers retain their explicit child restart policies.

Application scope retains only genuinely shared or independently owned infrastructure: Finch, the dynamic supervisor for control-point runtime roots, the independently owned IGD lease infrastructure, and the Registry described below. Control-point and eventing work must use the owning runtime task supervisor rather than a global one.

Retain `UPnP.Registry` with one concrete responsibility: resolve public control-point names/runtime handles and internal runtime component identities to the coordinator and owned supervisors. It owns no protocol state. Preserve both `{UPnP.ControlPoint, options}` and `UPnP.start_control_point/1`; public names and returned handles must continue to resolve through `UPnP.ControlPoint` APIs.

Graceful `UPnP.ControlPoint.close/2` first completes bounded GENA cleanup, then stops the runtime normally so it is not restarted. `UPnP.stop_control_point/1`, owner/supervisor loss, and crashes are abrupt: terminate the complete subtree without protocol goodbyes or orphan windows.

This records the required human topology and restart-strategy approval. Implementation is approved for AFK execution.

title: Remediate critical control-point defects from the 2026-07 audit
description:
## Why this epic exists

An adversarial four-lens audit (idiomatic Elixir, resilience, performance, security) of `upnp/lib`
found four Critical defects. All four were reproduced against running code, not merely inferred from
static reading.

Together they mean that **any host on the local network can permanently and silently disable a
`UPnP.ControlPoint` with a handful of unauthenticated UDP datagrams**, and that the application is
never told it has gone blind. There is no authentication, rate limit, recovery path, or failure
signal on this route.

The four children are:

1. bd-2cp, clamp untrusted SSDP `max-age` before it reaches `Process.send_after/3`.
2. bd-16w, make SSDP datagram parsing total, so a malformed `LOCATION` cannot raise.
3. bd-1e5, bound the presence roster and its per-entry BEAM timers.
4. bd-3nj, survive crash storms instead of exiting `:shutdown` and never restarting.

Children 1 and 2 remove the two known crash triggers. Child 3 removes the memory-exhaustion route.
Child 4 is the amplifier that turns any crash into a permanent, silent outage, and it will keep doing
so for the next crash bug unless it is addressed. Child 4 therefore depends on 1 and 2, and requires
human review before implementation because it changes restart and failure domains.

## Baselines at audit time

- `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`, `mix format --check-formatted`, `mix deps.unlock --check-unused`
  and `mix hex.audit` are all clean.
- `mix test` is 151 of 151, with one intermittent flake at `test/control_point_runtime_test.exs:180`.
- `mix credo` and `mix dialyzer` are **not** configured, so no static-analysis gate backstops any of
  this.

## Success Criteria

Applies to every child.

- [ ] `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` clean.
- [ ] `mix test` green.
- [ ] `mix format --check-formatted` clean.
- [ ] A regression test that **fails before** the fix and **passes after** it.
- [ ] Public documentation updated where it currently makes a claim the code does not honour.

The epic is done when a sustained flood of hostile SSDP datagrams leaves the control point alive,
resolvable, bounded in memory, and still serving its subscribers.

## Non-negotiable constraints

- Never modify the upstream libraries.
- Never weaken input validation, byte bounds, constant-time token comparison, or Saxy's
  `expand_entity: :keep` in order to make a test pass.
- Keep to the project time model: `TimeProvider` and the injected clock only, no wall-clock APIs.
- Tests must not depend on multicast, which does not work in the development container.
- Do not touch `samples/upnp_explorer/`, which is in-progress user work.

## Out of scope

Six High, fifteen Medium and eight Low findings from the same audit are recorded but deliberately not
filed here. Two verified High findings are cross-referenced from bd-3nj because they sit inside the
same failure window.

title: Harden :upnp OTP architecture and public interfaces
description:
## What to build

Bring the `:upnp` library from a strong idiomatic baseline to a consistently high-bar Elixir/OTP implementation. The campaign covers deterministic tests, supervision ownership, eventing Locality, canonical wire Interfaces, consistent Adapters, runtime policy cleanup, telemetry correctness, and the behavioral coverage gate.

This epic is complete only when every child slice is independently verified and the library presents one coherent ownership and Interface model.

- [ ] Concurrent test execution is deterministic at the repository default `max_cases`.
- [ ] Public documentation describes the final supervision, Adapter, and wire Interface contracts.
- [ ] No compatibility alias or globally supervised process remains without a documented reason.

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately

comments.author: Christian Geuer-Pollmann
comments.text: Human-gate review completed on 2026-07-26. The two decision-bearing children, bd-2vi and bd-dt3, now contain approved decisions and are labeled afk. This epic is a non-executable container, not human-gated work, so its hitl label is removed without adding afk. Close the epic only after all child acceptance criteria and final gates are complete.

title: Survive crash storms instead of silently and permanently destroying the control point
description:
## What to fix

This is the **amplifier** that turned two ordinary crash bugs into permanent, silent, remote denial of
service, and it will do the same to the next crash bug unless it is addressed.

`UPnP.ControlPoint.Runtime.init/1` at `lib/upnp/control_point/runtime.ex:119-131` uses
`strategy: :one_for_all` with `auto_shutdown: :any_significant` and **default, unconfigured** restart
intensity of 3 failures in 5 seconds. The coordinator child spec at
`lib/upnp/control_point/runtime.ex:133-142` is `restart: :transient` with `significant: true`.

The consequence chain is:

1. Any child crash restarts every child, discarding roster, subscriptions and caches.
2. Three crashes in five seconds exhaust intensity, and the supervisor exits with reason `:shutdown`.
3. `:transient` treats `:shutdown` as a **normal** exit, so the control point is **never restarted**.

Worse, the failure is silent. Verified after a flood: `Process.whereis(name)` returns `nil`, the
runtime is down with `:shutdown`, and the roster subscriber's mailbox length is **0**. Consumers
monitor nothing, and the coordinator only monitors *them*, so the application is never told it has
gone blind. For a long-running daemon, silent plus permanent is the worst combination.

## Two verified High findings inside the same failure window

Both were reproduced during the audit and both make the window more dangerous. Fix them as part of
this work or split them out deliberately, but do not lose them.

- `server/1` at `lib/upnp/control_point.ex:100-102` falls back to the **runtime supervisor pid** when
  `whereis/1` returns `nil`, which is exactly what happens during a restart. Verified: issuing a
  coordinator call against a Supervisor pid crashes the supervisor with `FunctionClauseError` in
  `:supervisor.handle_call/3` and kills the calling process too. So an ordinary public API call
  during the restart window destroys the runtime.
- `start_interfaces/2` at `lib/upnp/control_point.ex:710-734` caches `Interface` pids without
  monitoring them. `Interface` is `:transient`, so a `{:udp_error, _}` stop restarts it under a new
  pid. Verified: the next `search/2` exits `{:noproc, ...}` **inside the coordinator's
  `handle_call`**, killing the coordinator and burning a restart. Discovery stays broken until the
  runtime restarts.

## Human review required before implementation

This changes restart and failure domains, exactly like bd-2vi did. Agree the topology first, then
implement. Questions to settle:

- What are the correct intensity and period for a process fed by untrusted network traffic?
- Is `:one_for_all` right for children that do not actually share fate, such as one SSDP interface
  versus the eventing manager?
- Should the runtime be `:permanent` under a user supervisor, so exhaustion escalates rather than
  disappearing?
- What is the supported way for a consumer to observe control-point death: a documented monitor, a
  roster-subscription `:closed` signal, or both?

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Restart intensity and period are configured deliberately and the reasoning is documented.
- [ ] A sustained burst of crashing input no longer leaves the control point permanently absent.
- [ ] If the control point does stop for good, consumers receive an observable signal rather than
      silence.
- [ ] `server/1` never routes a coordinator call to a Supervisor pid.
- [ ] Cached `Interface` pids are monitored, or looked up rather than cached, so a restart cannot make
      the coordinator exit `:noproc`.
- [ ] A failure-injection test floods the control point with crashing datagrams and asserts it is
      still resolvable and still serving afterwards. It must fail before the fix.
- [ ] A test asserts a roster subscriber is notified when the control point dies.
- [ ] A test restarts an `Interface` and asserts a subsequent `search/2` succeeds without killing the
      coordinator.
- [ ] Documentation describes the restart semantics an embedder can rely on.

## Blocked by

Depends on the `max-age` clamp and on total SSDP parsing. Remove the two known crash triggers first,
so this work is verified against the residual class of failures rather than against those two bugs.

title: Centralize the UPnP protocol user-agent policy
description:
## Parent

bd-3lm

## What to build

Replace the five copies of `Elixir/#{System.version()} UPnP/2.0 upnp/0.1` in description, SCPD, SOAP action, SSDP, and GENA code with one protocol policy. The package version must come from authoritative application/build metadata rather than a second hardcoded value, and all outbound protocols must use the same default while retaining any intentional per-request override.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One implementation owns default user-agent composition.
- [ ] The emitted package version matches `mix.exs` and changes automatically with the package version.
- [ ] SSDP, description fetches, SCPD fetches, SOAP actions, and GENA subscriptions use the shared policy.
- [ ] Existing supported override behavior remains available and documented.
- [ ] Focused tests assert consistency and reject CR/LF injection in any caller-supplied value.
- [ ] No copied package-version or complete user-agent literal remains in `lib/`.

title: Make network routing a consistent injectable adapter
description:
## Parent

bd-3lm

## What to build

Turn network route selection into the same explicit Adapter seam used for HTTP, SSDP transport, GENA transport, and clocks. `UPnP.Eventing.Manager` currently probes `local_address_for/1` and `/2` with `function_exported?/3`, while `UPnP.IGD.Gateway` calls `UPnP.Network` directly and `UPnP.Options` exposes no route Adapter despite the README claiming route injection.

Define one callback contract, provide the system Adapter, carry it through validated control-point options, and use it consistently for callback-origin and IGD internal-client selection.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `UPnP.Network` declares a documented behavior with one callback shape.
- [ ] A system Adapter implements the behavior and preserves current kernel route-selection behavior.
- [ ] `UPnP.Options` validates and carries the configured route Adapter and its state/options.
- [ ] Eventing and IGD use the same Adapter seam; no `function_exported?/3` arity probing or direct hardcoded route lookup remains.
- [ ] Tests provide fake Adapters and cover success, missing route, wildcard address, IPv4 normalization, and Adapter failure without consulting the host route table.
- [ ] README injection claims match the implemented Interface.

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately

title: Canonicalize public wire-format interfaces
description:
## Parent

bd-3lm

## What to build

Choose and enforce one canonical Interface for each public wire format. The current surface exposes parallel routes through `UPnP.SOAP`, `UPnP.SOAP.Parser`, `UPnP.SOAP.Composer`, `UPnP.Description`, parser aliases such as `parse_device_description/2`, and the unused `UPnP.Eventing.AV.Parser` delegate. Several recommended facade modules have no direct tests.

Apply the deletion test: retain a facade only when it hides meaningful implementation knowledge. Align source paths with module names and separate multiple public modules currently defined in one file. Because this may remove public functions in version 0.1, obtain human approval for the canonical names and compatibility policy before implementation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A reviewed table identifies the canonical Module and function names for description, SCPD, SOAP, GENA property-set, SSDP, and AV LastChange formats.
- [ ] Each operation has one documented public entry point; redundant delegates and aliases are removed or explicitly deprecated.
- [ ] Implementation-only parser/composer modules are hidden from generated documentation when they are not part of the Interface.
- [ ] Public tests call the canonical Interfaces rather than bypassing them for implementation modules.
- [ ] File paths conventionally mirror module names, including a separate file for `UPnP.AllowedValueRange`.
- [ ] README and ExDoc examples use only canonical names.

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately
close_reason: Resolved in e10cc0d. Canonical wire formats now expose the approved documented entry points; redundant delegates are removed and retained directional modules are hidden. Regression: test/wire_interface_test.exs.

comments.author: Christian Geuer-Pollmann
comments.text:
Human decision approved on 2026-07-26:

Use idiomatic semantic domain modules as the canonical public wire interfaces. Domain modules should own parsing/composition directly where practical; do not retain facade-only delegates. A facade is justified for SOAP and SSDP because each meaningfully unifies composition and parsing while hiding the internal directional split.

Canonical table:
- Device description: `UPnP.Description.parse/2`
- SCPD: `UPnP.SCPD.parse/1`
- SOAP: `UPnP.SOAP.compose/3`, `UPnP.SOAP.soap_action_header/2`, `UPnP.SOAP.parse/2`, and `UPnP.SOAP.parse_fault/1`
- GENA property set: `UPnP.Eventing.PropertySet.parse/1`
- SSDP: `UPnP.SSDP.parse/1` and `UPnP.SSDP.m_search/2`
- AV LastChange: `UPnP.Eventing.AV.LastChange.parse/1`

Implementation-only parser/composer modules may remain internally when they provide real separation, but must be hidden from ExDoc and are not public contracts. Remove redundant aliases and delegates, including `parse_device_description/2`, `parse_scpd/1`, SOAP long-form aliases, `parse_property_set/1`, and the unused `UPnP.Eventing.AV.Parser` delegate. Public tests, README, and ExDoc examples must use only the canonical table. Split `UPnP.AllowedValueRange` into its conventionally named file.

Compatibility policy: hard-remove the redundant pre-1.0 surface now, with no shims or deprecation cycle. If a 0.1.x package has already been published, expose this break in the next minor release rather than a patch.

This records the required human naming and compatibility approval. Implementation is approved for AFK execution.

title: Make concurrent eventing tests deterministic
description:
## Parent

bd-3lm

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `mix test --seed 971129 --max-cases 48`.
2. Observe timeouts at `test/eventing_transport_test.exs:42` and `test/eventing_integration_test.exs:69`; the run has reproduced as 75/77.
3. Run the same seed with `--max-cases 1` and observe 77/77 passing.
4. Run each failing test repeatedly in isolation and observe it passing, confirming scheduler-load sensitivity rather than a deterministic assertion failure.

## What to build

Remove scheduler-load sensitivity from the asynchronous eventing tests without weakening their assertions or hiding races behind sleeps. Use explicit process handshakes, monitors, or deliberately bounded receive timeouts for cross-process startup. Ensure failed assertions cannot leave subscription workers running after their manual clock has been torn down.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `mix test --seed 971129 --max-cases 48` passes repeatedly under concurrent execution.
- [ ] The eventing transport and integration tests synchronize on observable messages rather than incidental scheduler timing.
- [ ] No `Process.sleep/1` or unbounded retry loop is introduced.
- [ ] A test failure or timeout cleans up spawned tasks and workers without subsequent GenServer crash logs.
- [ ] The full suite retains `async: true` wherever state is genuinely isolated.

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately
close_reason: Resolved in 91cf647. Eventing tests now use supervised tasks and explicit bounded message handshakes; canceled callers drain workers before clock teardown. Regression: an aborted subscription caller cannot leave its eventing worker behind.
